name: Julius Maternus to Agisymba
summary: A Roman from Leptis Magna travels south with the king of the Garamantes, four months across the Sahara to Agisymba, a land 'where the rhinoceroses gather'. Ptolemy took his account from the geographer Marinus; where Agisymba lay, perhaps near Lake Chad, is unknown.

stops.note: Maternus sets out from the coast of Tripolitania.
The capital of the Garamantes, desert traders and charioteers of the Fezzan.
Four months to the south with the Garamantian king, to a land of rhinoceroses.
Home with the farthest report of Africa Rome ever had.
